claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component authors can change a component's internal design and include the state migration in the same release.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the component state migration callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repo contains aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration with v1, v2 and v3 programs and migration code.
The example's migration files exist at aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration/v2/migration.ts and v3/migration.ts in pulumi/examples.
The legacy awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc component in the example creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Per the AWS CloudFormation docs, the security group's VpcId property change requires replacement of the security group, so a new VPC would mean replacing the security group.
If a database is recreated, its replacement does not automatically contain the old data.
The modern component is awsx.ec2.Vpc.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with @pulumi/aws.
Across all three versions of the example the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
In the example, the Pulumi resource tree for v1 uses awsx:x:ec2:Vpc, v2 uses awsx:ec2:Vpc, and v3 uses plain aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc, with the subnet named vpc-isolated-1 in v2 and v3.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, modern AWSX removes those wrappers, and the subnet's Pulumi name changes from vpc-isolated-0 to vpc-isolated-1.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot by themselves remove component wrappers and transfer references.
A component registers a migration via the stateMigrations resource option together with an alias for the legacy component type.

The state migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns newState (complete set of replacement records) and successors (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that replaces it).
The example's rename helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses successors mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a modern AWSX stack skips the first migration, and after both run later updates return no result.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
pulumi preview evaluates the state migration without saving it, and pulumi up saves the migrated state.

When users upgrade a component that registers a state migration, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of normal preview and update, without users writing the migration or editing stack state.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.

A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings, where each mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
Component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
The Pulumi option reference at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API for state migrations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
In Pulumi, the restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
